subject: QuantifAI SLO check-in: token ceilings & streaming commitments
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Luke Harris <luke@quantifai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: QuantifAI SLO check-in: token ceilings & streaming commitments

Hi Luke —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned on scope and measurement for the POC: 

Summary (what we heard)
- Target p95 user-observed latency: 150ms for typical requests; flexible for long-context cases.
- Concurrency target: baseline 50 sustained concurrent sessions, spiky bursts to 150 for short periods.
- Typical request shape: 70% short (<=512 tokens in), 25% mid (512-2048 in), 5% long (>2048 in). Output avg ~128 tokens, worst-case 1024.
- Streaming required for UI use-case (progressive token emission to reduce perceived latency).
- Sensitive fields flagged — QuantifAI needs SOC2 controls and audit logs (we discussed KMS/HSM options).

Immediate asks from Redwood
- Please share representative prompt set and a small sample of logs (anonymized) so we can run shape analysis. You mentioned a CSV; attaching our sample mapping template.
- Confirm the absolute max context we should support in the POC (you mentioned 8192 tokens as likely ceiling — please confirm).
- Procurement/POC contact and expected timing for a short Dedicated canary vs hosted test.

Suggested POC measurement plan (high level)
- Baseline: host model variant M-medium (float16) with prefix caching enabled.
- Tests: three 10-min ramps at target concurrencies (10 / 50 / 150) with mixed prompt distribution.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (server and client-observed), tokens/sec, KV cache hit rate, batching sizes, and failure modes when >max tokens.
- Streaming: run an A/B to compare full-response vs streaming token-by-token for tail latency.

Next steps
- You: share sample prompts & procurement contact by EOD Thursday (2027-08-05).
- Us: we’ll produce a POC config (+ expected cost estimate) and a canary runbook by Friday.

Attachments: quantifai_sample_prompts.csv (format we prefer).

Thanks — happy to sync over a quick 30m if helpful.

—
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

From: Luke Harris <luke@quantifai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Ops Team <ops@quantifai.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QuantifAI SLO check-in: token ceilings & streaming commitments

Camila — thanks for the crisp notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

On context sizes
- We can commit to the 8192 token ceiling for the POC, but ~10% of requests will push into the 10k+ range for analytics jobs (those can be batched offline). For interactive UI, 8k is the hard target.

On latency targets
- Our goal is 150ms p95 for the interactive UI for requests <=1024 input tokens and <=256 output. For longer contexts (2k+ in), we expect a relaxed target — upper bound 400ms p95 is acceptable if we have streaming.

Fallback/behavior on token overflow
- For requests that exceed the ceiling we prefer an explicit 413-style error with suggested client-side summarization guidance rather than silent truncation.

Compliance
- Procurement asked for our SOC2 addendum & security questionnaire answers; I’m attaching the security Q&A we keep internally for vendors.

Procurement
- Please route billing/POC order to procurement@quantifai.com (cc’ing them now). We’re aiming to start POC the week of Aug 16.

Quick question: for the streaming option, will Redwood guarantee that partial output is committed to logs/audit even if the session is interrupted? We need traceability.

Thanks — Luke
Luke Harris
Head of Platform, QuantifAI
luke@quantifai.com

[Attached: security_qanda.docx]
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Luke Harris <luke@quantifai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Ops Team <ops@quantifai.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QuantifAI SLO check-in: token ceilings & streaming commitments

Luke — great, thanks for the clarifications. A few commitments and concrete answers below.

1) Max context and overflow handling
- POC config will honor an 8192 token ceiling for interactive routes. For requests above that we will return a 413 plus a short JSON payload with an explain/summarize suggestion (client guidance). We will include a recommended client-side summarization snippet for your frontend team.

2) Latency expectations by bucket (server-observed p95) — rough guidance we’ll validate in canary:
- Short (<=512 in / <=256 out): 100–140ms p95
- Mid (512–1024 in / <=512 out): 140–220ms p95
- Long (1024–8192 in / 256–1024 out): 220–400ms p95 (streaming enabled to keep perceived latency low)

3) Streaming and audit logs
- Streaming: Redwood will stream tokens as they are generated to clients (SSE/WebSocket) and we’ll persist the final generated text plus streaming token events to the audit log. If a session is interrupted, partial streams remain in logs for traceability.

4) Measurement/canary proposal
- Canary topology: 3 dedicated GPU workers, batching window tuned to 10–20ms, KV cache prewarm from sample prompts.
- Tests: ramp scenario at 10/50/150 concurrency with your sample set. We’ll produce a single CSV of per-request latencies and token counts so you can ingest into your monitoring.

5) Cost/ops note
- We’ll include two options in the POC proposal: hosted with reserved concurrency (fast to start) and a 3-node Dedicated canary (predictable latency, lower p99 tails).

Next actions
- We’ll draft the runbook + SLO table and share by Friday.
- Camila: can you confirm procurement contact? (Luke already cc’d)

Attachments added: SLO_proposal_v1.pdf (initial runbook & expected metrics).

—
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: QuantifAI SLO check-in: token ceilings & streaming commitments

Camila — quick internal note: I’m good with the 3-node canary as long as we instrument KV cache hit rate and expose batching histograms to their team. Set default batching window to 15ms, enable prefix caching. I’ll own the runbook exec.

—Markus

markus@redwood.com
